description: Audit an agent's claim that work is complete by mapping each claim to observed repository, test, UI, API, or remote evidence. Use before saying done, shipped, fixed, pushed, or verified.
name: completion-claims-auditor

description: Establish a known-good baseline and protect unrelated working behavior before AI edits an established project. Use before risky fixes, refactors, or broad feature work.
name: existing-work-preservation

description: Audit MCP/plugin tool integrations for startup cost, health, retries, timeouts, process leaks, permission scope, and failure isolation. Use when agents stall, spawn processes, or load many MCP servers.
name: mcp-reliability-auditor

description: Integrate parallel agent changes by detecting file overlap, incompatible assumptions, duplicated implementations, semantic conflicts, and missing combined tests. Use before merging worker branches or worktrees.
name: multi-agent-integration-reviewer

description: Reconstruct an interrupted project's goals, current state, completed work, and next safe actions from repository evidence. Use after context loss, compaction, session changes, or handoff.
name: project-context-recovery

description: Map a large prompt, specification, or issue into stable requirements and verify each against implementation and evidence. Use for complex multi-requirement work or final audits.
name: requirement-traceability-auditor

description: Detect edits outside the requested change surface and require a dependency rationale for every additional file. Use during or after autonomous code changes.
name: scope-drift-guard

description: Find modules whose coupling, size, responsibility mix, or change fan-out makes AI-assisted maintenance fragile. Use before major refactors or when files keep growing.
name: architecture-complexity-auditor

description: Detect direct and indirect module dependency cycles and choose the smallest safe boundary to break them. Use for circular imports, layering failures, or tangled module graphs.
name: dependency-cycle-auditor

description: Review multi-step writes, retries, concurrency, and idempotency for lost updates, duplicates, partial state, and race conditions. Use for payments, jobs, counters, workflows, or shared records.
name: data-consistency-auditor

description: Review relational or document schemas for keys, relationships, constraints, nullability, indexes, and access-pattern fit. Use before schema creation or migration.
name: database-schema-reviewer

description: Audit database migrations for destructive changes, locking, backfill, rollback, and mixed-version rollout safety. Use before applying schema/data migrations.
name: migration-safety-reviewer

description: Detect and stop no-progress debugging, retry, and tool-call loops while preserving repeated actions that make measurable progress. Use when the same action or error is recurring.
name: loop-breaker

description: Create the smallest reliable reproducer for a reported software failure before attempting a fix. Use when a bug is intermittent, environment-sensitive, or not covered by a failing test.
name: reproduction-builder

description: Diagnose recurring software failures from reproducible evidence, logs, failing tests, and causal hypotheses. Use when a bug fix is uncertain, repeated, or risks treating symptoms.
name: root-cause-debugger

description: Verify proposed packages, versions, imports, and upgrade claims against project state and authoritative package metadata. Use before adding or changing a dependency.
name: dependency-grounding-auditor

description: Diagnose failing CI jobs from the exact failing step, logs, environment, and reproducible local checks. Use when a pipeline fails or an agent proposes speculative workflow edits.
name: ci-failure-investigator

description: Find shell, path, case, newline, permission, encoding, and runtime assumptions that break on Windows, macOS, or Linux. Use for cross-platform projects or platform-specific failures.
name: cross-platform-readiness-auditor

description: Derive required configuration keys from code and manifests, detect missing/unused/misspelled variables, and verify fail-fast behavior. Use for environment-variable or deployment configuration changes.
name: environment-config-auditor

description: Compare local, CI, container, and production assumptions for runtime versions, dependencies, services, paths, and build/start commands. Use when software works locally but fails elsewhere.
name: environment-parity-auditor

description: Audit a service or application for deployability, health/readiness, logging, failure behavior, backup/recovery assumptions, and critical smoke checks. Use before a release or production handoff.
name: production-readiness-auditor

description: Verify README, setup, examples, commands, API docs, screenshots/claims, and paths against the current repository. Use after implementation or before release.
name: documentation-accuracy-auditor

description: Reduce repeated context, research, tool calls, and overengineering while preserving verification quality. Use when an agent is rereading the same material or spending heavily on low-value exploration.
name: token-efficient-workflow

description: Audit interactive UI for semantic structure, keyboard/focus behavior, accessible names, contrast, motion, and touch targets. Use for UI changes or accessibility review.
name: accessibility-auditor

description: Trace visible controls, routes, commands, and integrations to real handlers and observable effects to find placeholders or hardcoded demos. Use before declaring a product feature complete.
name: dead-feature-detector

description: Verify changed UI across representative viewport widths for overflow, clipping, reflow, navigation, touch targets, and content priority. Use for frontend layout changes.
name: responsive-design-auditor

description: Audit user flows for loading, empty, success, validation, partial, permission, offline, and error states. Use when async UI or data-driven workflows are added.
name: ux-state-completeness-auditor

description: Cross-check version metadata, changelog, tags, packaged artifacts, install/start behavior, and publication workflow before or after a release. Use for release preparation or audit.
name: release-verification-agent

description: Review tool-using agent workflows for prompt injection, untrusted-content authority confusion, excessive permissions, and unsafe action boundaries. Use when agents read external content and can mutate systems.
name: agent-tool-trust-auditor

description: Audit authentication flows for server-side identity verification, session/token handling, and bypass paths. Use when login, session, OAuth, API-key, or protected-route code changes.
name: authentication-security-auditor

description: Audit object, action, role, and tenant authorization boundaries after identity is established. Use for permissions, ownership, admin, organization, or multi-user features.
name: authorization-boundary-auditor

description: Review dependency additions and upgrades for known vulnerabilities, risky provenance, and unnecessary supply-chain exposure. Use for dependency changes or security audits.
name: dependency-vulnerability-auditor

description: Trace untrusted input into SQL, shell, template, path, and other interpreter sinks. Use for security review or changes involving dynamic queries/commands.
name: injection-risk-auditor

description: Audit server-side validation at trust boundaries for shape, type, range, format, size, and semantic constraints. Use for APIs, forms, uploads, imports, or external events.
name: input-validation-auditor

description: Detect likely credentials, private keys, tokens, and secret-bearing configuration before commit or publication. Use for security review, pre-push checks, or suspicious configuration changes.
name: secret-leakage-detector

description: Inspect runtime, web, container, and deployment configuration for unsafe production defaults. Use before release or when CORS, cookies, debug mode, network exposure, TLS, or headers change.
name: security-misconfiguration-auditor

description: Compare API producers, consumers, schemas, types, status codes, and error shapes to detect contract drift. Use for client/server changes or API versioning.
name: api-contract-auditor

description: Identify critical integrations proven only by mocks and design the smallest realistic contract or sandbox verification. Use for APIs, databases, queues, storage, auth providers, or external services.
name: integration-reality-checker

description: Map changed or critical behavior to automated checks and identify meaningful untested paths. Use after feature work, bug fixes, or when coverage appears misleading.
name: missing-test-detector

description: Detect behavior regressions introduced by a change by comparing baselines, requirements, tests, and adjacent flows. Use after a fix, refactor, dependency change, or generated patch.
name: regression-detector

description: Detect skipped, vacuous, over-mocked, implementation-mirroring, and nondeterministic tests that create false confidence. Use when a suite is green but quality is uncertain.
name: test-quality-auditor

description: Verify real user flows in a browser across navigation, forms, async states, and errors. Use when a visible frontend feature is added or claimed complete.
name: ui-flow-verifier
